question: the bulk sap glucose at the bore wall below which 85's stagnant sap gap cannot carry the node's cold-start and sleep draws, and what binds first in that gap
model: necessary: C_nec = I/S, S = n·F·D·A/δ on the side that keeps «below X it cannot» true (bottom cap added, D + U, the draw's low end; rounded down); S_uA_per_mM = [envelope at D − U, with the cap at D + U]; series estimate C* = I/S + K_M·I/(J_max·A − I) on the envelope at D and the draw's high end, per Ea

verdict: Necessary, not sufficient: below 0.09–0.32 mM of glucose at the bore wall (20 °C, across the Zone-1 parts; 0.17–0.59 mM at 0 °C) a stagnant sap gap cannot carry the cold-start draw (25.0 µA) for any enzyme, glucose being the only substrate. In the same gap the face first leaves the enzyme's measured pH window: 31 of 35 draw×part pairs exceed, in every reading, the current at which 85's face leaves the enzyme's kinetic bracket (pH 5.5) at 25 °C, and on pine the cold start reaches pH 4.5 in some readings — so sap above the threshold does not by itself keep the face inside that window.
cannot_see: whether a living stem keeps the gap stagnant (flow raises the supply; ingrowth has no source)
glucose consumed on the way by wood cells or microbes (raises the threshold)
the α-anomer: the enzyme oxidises β-D-glucose, slow mutarotation raises the threshold
xylose, the enzyme's other substrate (lowers it, if present)
the bore wall's own resistance — embolised tracheids, resin (raises it)
temperatures between 0 and 20 °C except as a bracket; the proton half below 25 °C
the enzyme ceiling on etched Ti in sap; whether the envelope area over- or understates the kinetic term (not established — the series estimate carries no direction)
